extracted.intended_audience: designers, engravers, printers, proprietors, and legal practitioners concerned with 18th-century British copyright/related statutes
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of legal provisions governing copyright-like protections for prints, engravings, book bequests, textile patterns, and models/casts in 18th‑century Great Britain (statutory rights, registration, limitations, remedies, and procedural rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for protection for prints and engravings
rubrics_metrics.description: 'From and after the first day of January, One thousand seven hundred and sixty-seven, all and every person and persons who shall invent or design, engrave, etch, or ... work in mezzotinto or chiaro oscuro ... any historical print or prints, or any print or prints ... shall have, and are hereby declared to have, the benefit and protection of the said act and this act, under the restrictions and limitations hereinafter mentioned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants statutory protection to creators/causers-of-creation of prints (including mezzotinto/chiaro oscuro). Protection is subject to the act's specific restrictions and time limits described elsewhere in the statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection extends to prints taken from pictures/drawings/models/sculptures
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That ... all and every person and persons who shall engrave, etch, or work in mezzotinto or chiaro oscuro, or cause to be engraved, etched, or worked, any print taken from any picture, drawing, model, or sculpture, either ancient or modern, shall have, and are hereby declared to have, the benefit and protection of the said act, and this act, for the term hereinafter mentioned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly covers prints that reproduce other works (paintings, drawings, models, sculptures) — treating such engravings as entitled to the same statutory protection and term as original engravings under the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability and penalties for unauthorised copying/printing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'If any person shall engrave, print, and publish, or import for sale, any copy of any such print, contrary to the true intent and meaning of this and the said former act, every such person shall be liable to the penalties contained in the said act... to be recovered as therein and hereinafter is mentioned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorised copying/printing/importing triggers statutory penalties and civil remedies as specified in the earlier and current acts; enforcement mechanisms and recovery rules are set out elsewhere in the statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive/right term for proprietors (prints) — twenty and twenty‑eight years
rubrics_metrics.description: (earlier clause) 'The sole right of printing and reprinting the late F. Hogarth's prints, vested in his widow and executrix for twenty years.'; (later clause) 'the sole right and liberty of printing and reprinting ... shall be extended, continued, and be vested in the respective proprietors, for the space of twenty‑eight years, to commence from the day of the first publishing ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets limited exclusive terms for printing/reprinting particular works (examples: 20 years in specific grant; generally extended to 28 years from first publication). Terms determine period of enforceable exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery procedure and plaintiff's costs when enforcing penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: 'All and every the penalties and penalty inflicted by the said act ... shall and may be sued for and recovered in like manner, and under the like restrictions and limitations, as in and by the said act is declared and appointed; and the plaintiff or common informer ... shall recover the same, together with his full costs of suit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties recoverable by action (including by common informer) and plaintiff may recover full costs; recovery follows procedures and limitations in the referenced earlier statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to commence prosecution (six calendar months)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Provided also, That the party prosecuting shall commence his prosecution within the space of six calendar months after the offence committed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory limitation: enforcement actions for specified offences must be begun within six months of the offending act; repeated in several acts for actions related to prints and textile-pattern offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defence procedure: general issue and special matter; costs to defendants on successful defence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The defendant or defendants ... shall or may plead the general issue, and give the special matter in evidence; and if upon such action or suit, a verdict shall be given for the defendant ... then the defendant or defendants shall have and recover full costs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendants may plead the general issue and introduce special matter as evidence; if defendant succeeds or plaintiff discontinues, defendant recovers full costs (remedy like other civil actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities/colleges may hold copyright in perpetuity for bequeathed books
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That the said universities and colleges respectively shall, at their respective presses, have, for ever, the sole liberty of printing and reprinting all such [books] which have been, or shall at any time hereafter be bequeathed, or otherwise given by the author or authors ... to or in trust for the said universities ... for the purposes aforesaid, unless the same shall have been bequeathed or given for any term of years, or other limited term.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perpetual exclusive printing/reprinting rights are granted to universities/colleges for books bequeathed to them for educational purposes, unless the bequest specified a limited term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition that university/college printing be at their own presses — delegation voids privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nothing in this act extend to grant any exclusive right, otherwise than so long as the books or copies belonging to the said universities or colleges are printed only at their own printing presses within the said universities or colleges respectively, and for their sole benefit and advantage; and that if any university or college shall delegate, grant, lease, or sell their copyrights ... then the privileges hereby granted are to become void and of no effect.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perpetual right is conditional: printing must be performed at the institution's own presses for its sole benefit; delegating or assigning the copyright/printing rights voids the statutory privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to enter title in Stationers' register to trigger forfeitures/penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nothing in this act shall be construed to extend to subject any bookseller, printer, or other person whatsoever, to the forfeitures or penalties herein mentioned, ... unless the title to the copy of such book ... be entered in the register book of the Company of Stationers ... on or before the twenty-fourth day of June One thousand seven hundred and seventy five; and of all such book or books as may or shall hereafter be bequeathed or given as aforesaid, be entered in such register within the space of two months after any such bequest or gift shall have come to the knowledge of the vice-chancellors ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To trigger statutory forfeitures/penalties regarding bequeathed books, the book's title must be entered in the Stationers' register within specified deadlines (historic date for existing bequests; two months for future bequests). Entry fee set at sixpence per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register inspection and certification; clerk's penalty for refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The said Register Book shall ... be inspected by any bookseller ...; the clerk of the said Company of Stationers shall, when required, give a certificate ... and for every such certificate may take a fee ... not exceeding sixpence. That if the Clerk ... shall refuse or neglect to register or make such entry ... or to give such certificate ... the clerk ... shall, for every such offence, forfeit twenty pounds to the proprietor or proprietors of every such copyright.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides public inspection of register, limited certificate fee (≤6d), and penalizes clerk's refusal to register with a £20 forfeiture payable to the proprietor; recovery by action in courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine-copy deposit requirement for printed books (royal/university libraries) and completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Text of act: earlier requirement of nine copies on best paper to warehouse-keeper for specified libraries; later amendment requires entry of title for whole book and delivery of nine copies of whole work to warehouse-keeper.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory public‑act status and judicial notice
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That this act shall be adjudged, deemed, and taken to be a public act; and shall be judicially taken notice of as such by all Judges, Justices, and other persons whatsoever, without specially pleading the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutes are public acts and courts are to take judicial notice of them without special pleading — procedural consequence for litigants and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent formalities required for lawful copying/printing (prints and textile patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: (17 Geo. III & textile acts) '... without the express consent of the proprietor or proprietors thereof first had and obtained in writing, signed by him, her, or them respectively, with his, her, or their own hand or hands, in the presence of, and attested by, two or more credible witnesses, then every such proprietor or proprietors shall ... recover such damages ... together with double costs of suit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To lawfully make, vary, print, reprint, or publish copies of protected prints/patterns, written consent signed and attested by two credible witnesses is required; lack of such consent entitles proprietor to damages and (in some acts) double costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive short‑term protection for textile patterns (printing rights and marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: (27 Geo. III c.38) '... every person who shall invent, design, and print ... any new and original pattern or patterns for printing linens, cottons, calicoes, or muslins, shall have the sole right of printing and reprinting the same for the term of two months, to commence from the day of the first publishing thereof, which shall be truly printed, with the name of the printer or proprietors at each end of every such piece ...' (34 Geo. III later: term extended to three months and made perpetual in other respects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers/printers of new textile patterns enjoy a short statutory exclusive period (two months initially, later three months) from first publication; pieces must bear the printer/proprietor's name at each end. Remedies for copying during the term include special action for damages and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy and mode of action for infringement of textile patterns and related offences
rubrics_metrics.description: 'If any calico printer, linen-draper, or other person ... shall ... print, work, or copy such original pattern ... knowing the same to be so printed or reprinted without the consent of the proprietor ... then every such proprietor ... shall, if the offence be committed in England, by and in a special action upon the case ... recover such damages as a jury ... shall give or assess, together with costs of suit ... and if the offence be committed in Scotland, ... by an action before the Court of Session ... recover such damages ... and for payment whereof decree shall be issued, with full costs of suit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement of textile-pattern rights gives the proprietor a civil action (special action in England; Court of Session in Scotland) to recover jury-assessed damages and full costs; procedural limitations on pleas and allowances (no wager, limited essoin, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation/continuation provisions for temporary Acts (textile patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'This act shall continue in force for one year, and from thence to the end of the then next session of parliament; and shall be deemed, adjudged, and taken to be a public act.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Acts granting pattern protection were initially temporary (one year plus remainder of session), subject to extension, repeal, or being made perpetual by later Acts (as occurred with later statutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of makers of new models and casts (busts/statues)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That from and after the passing of this Act, every person who shall make or cause to be made any new model, or copy or cast made from such new model, or any bust, or any part of the human figure, or any statue of the human figure, or the head ... shall be [vested with the sole property] ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory exclusive property rights to makers of new models/casts of busts, statues, and similar three-dimensional works, to prevent copying/moulding without consent and to encourage model-making arts; remedies for copying follow in the remainder of the act.
